column2:
Do you have a methodology in place to measure the impact of open data in your country?
 
For Explanation:
* If yes, please briefly describe the key points of this methodology.
column4:
Methodology is developed in partnership with UNDP, in 2019. URL (linked also on the National Open Data Portal) https://www.undp.org/sr/serbia/publications/potencijalni-uticaj-otvaranja-podataka-u-srbiji  Framework for open data impact indicators  which is proposed in this methodology  is
based on several dimensions.
First the dimension of balancing lead and lag indicators. Lead indicators show whether the right
things to enable open data impact are happening (as no impact would be possible otherwise),
and lag indicators to assess what impact is visible.
Second, establishing indicators along the entire value chain that leads to socio-economic impact
of open data, as apparent from the reviewed research. This value chain runs from data provision,
government efficiency gains, demand and adoption, time and resource investment by external
stakeholders, re-use examples, policy implementation, ecosystem formation, to higher order
usage and network effects.
For the different steps in that chain, both lead and lag indicators can be put forward, along with
the methods to measure them where such experience exists in the research taken into account.
Third, indicators as much as possible should be of the ‘vector’ type (measuring direction and
speed), which more likely leads to more objective measurements. The exact list of indicators is available starting from page 53 of the publication.

column7:
One of the applications uses data on accesibility in the city of Bor, from crowdsourcing. It raises the awareness on need to change the infrastructure in this city. URL to the reuse case: https://pristupacnostbor.com/ URL to data: https://data.gov.rs/sr/datasets/mapa-pristupachnosti-za-osobe-sa-invaliditetom-grada-bora/ Description and impact of the reuse case: The goal is to enable visibility of issues faced by persons with disabilities in the city of Bor through a GIS application with a crowdsourcing component.

The mobile and web application will allow citizens to view, enter, and modify data, providing an opportunity for persons with disabilities and all residents of Bor to mark locations on the map, add photos, provide descriptions, and offer suggestions to improve the accessibility of urban and traffic infrastructure in the city of Bor.

In this way, persons with disabilities will be able to actively and directly participate in the urban planning of the city, making their problems visible to the broader community and ensuring that their voices and issues are heard by decision-makers in the City Administration of Bor. Decision-makers (City Administration of Bor, Urban Planning Department of Bor, Road Management of Bor, Inspection Department of Bor, Police Department of Bor, Road Safety Council of Bor, etc.) will be obliged to respond to the existing problems and ensure the accessibility of traffic and urban infrastructure for persons with disabilities.

With this application, the goal is to engage and involve experts in the decision-making process.

Long-term goal is for the city of Bor to adopt and implement an effective and sustainable traffic safety strategy, adopt a sustainable urban mobility plan, and shape the traffic space through the application of "Humane Engineering" to ensure the accessibility of public spaces for end users.

Direct beneficiaries: Persons with disabilities and related associations.
Indirect beneficiaries: City Administration of Bor, Urban Planning Department of Bor, Road Management of Bor, Inspection Department of Bor, Police Department of Bor, Road Safety Council of Bor, citizens of Bor.

column7:
Several applications are developed in the area of healthcare. One of them is Medtest.io, application providing info on safety and dosage in prescribing medicines URL: https://data.gov.rs/sr/organizations/kneesearch-gmbh-2/  Dataset URL: https://data.gov.rs/sr/datasets/lekovi-za-upotrebu-u-khumanoj-meditsini/ Description: The former research group for e-Medication at Inselspital, University of Bern, in collaboration with local experts, has launched a project to establish an online portal for checking the safety of medication prescribing and dosing in our region. The idea of this project is to create user-friendly, portable, and always accessible software that assists in prescribing and dosing medications.
MedTest is a modern response to the volume and complexity of information faced by healthcare professionals and patients, especially given the increasing number of medications in use and the growing number of pathological conditions in patients.
MedTest consolidates this complexity through its functions of verification, notifications, and recommendations, clearly outlining risk profiles in a structured and concise manner.
In collaboration with Avoxa - Mediengruppe Deutscher Apotheker GmbH.  The other example is Covid 19 statistics visualization, developed by the Office for IT and eGovernment, which was highly relevant during the peak in the pandemic (https://covid19.data.gov.rs/?locale=en). Datatset URL: https://data.gov.rs/sr/datasets/covid-19-dnevni-izveshtaj-instituta-za-javno-zdravlje-srbije-o-zarazhenim-litsima-na-teritoriji-republike-srbije/ Description: The Office for IT and eGovernment has made available data and statistics on the number of citizens in self-isolation, those infected with the COVID-19 virus, as well as those tested, hospitalized, and deceased within the territory of the Republic of Serbia.

Data on the number of individuals in self-isolation and those infected are available through the visualization of these figures by municipalities and cities, starting from the moment when the first official case of COVID-19 was recorded in Serbia.

All data can be exported in xls and csv formats for further analysis and visualization.
